us-midterms.title: In the United States, Election Day in the midterms is marked by the struggle for control of Congress and Justice Department involvement
us-midterms.summary: Midterm elections have begun in the United States, and their outcome will determine control of Congress for the remainder of Donald Trump’s second term. The reports say all 435 House seats and one-third of the Senate are being contested, as well as some governorships; the publications describe the balance of power differently, but agree that the vote will decide which party controls Congress. A number of articles separately note record-high early voting and heightened attention from observers at polling places. TASS recalls that the party of the sitting president has lost seats in Congress in such elections only three times in the past 92 years.
us-midterms.picture: The drawing shows a giant ballot box standing on a cracked pedestal, while rivals on either side reach for documents and campaign posters. The scales of justice above underscore that the fight is not only for votes, but also for legal and political control.

iran-hormuz.title: The United States strikes Iranian targets, and the Strait of Hormuz again becomes a flashpoint for a major war
iran-hormuz.summary: Media reported that the United States carried out limited strikes on the Iranian island of Qeshm in the Strait of Hormuz. According to American sources, these were “defensive” strikes on sites linked to the use of anti-aircraft missiles against U.S. forces; Iran, in turn, said a deal with the United States was still out of reach. The reports note that the strikes came on the eve of the midterm elections in the United States and heightened anxiety in oil markets and over security in the Strait of Hormuz.

The Ukrainian and Russian sides are also trading accusations over violations of energy-related agreements. Against the backdrop of the attacks, the articles record deaths and injuries as well as new damage to civilian infrastructure.

binance-hack.title: After the biggest hack, Binance is trying to preserve trust and stop the outflow of funds
binance-hack.summary: After the largest hack of the Binance crypto exchange, the company is trying to restore customer trust and show that it has enough resources to weather the crisis. Reuters quotes the co-CEO as saying its financial position is “very strong,” while other reports say that after the theft of roughly $6.3 billion, users were able to recover their funds within days. At the same time, U.S. agencies and cyber analysts blame North Korea, while Pyongyang denies it and calls the accusations a provocation. Questions also remain about how exactly the hack was carried out and who was behind it.

israel-election.title: Israel remains in a political deadlock as rival camps seek a new majority
israel-election.summary: After a tense election in Israel, the political deadlock continues: neither Gadi Eisenkot’s camp nor Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc won a clear majority. The opposition is discussing uniting around Eisenkot, while Netanyahu himself says voters chose him; meanwhile, his camp is reportedly trying to delay confirmation of the results. Another thread is whether Jewish opposition parties are ready to rely on Arab factions, which could become decisive in forming a coalition. President Isaac Herzog, according to The Hindu, called on politicians to accept the result and find a way out so as not to drag the country into new elections.

Reuters, AFP, AP and other outlets agree that Washington says the countries failed to meet participation criteria, while The New York Times adds that the Trump administration accuses South Africa of discriminating against white people. fridge-cyberattacks.title: A new wave of cyberattacks in Europe is taking supermarket refrigeration systems offline
fridge-cyberattacks.summary: A new wave of cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration systems has been recorded in several European countries. AP, Reuters, AFP and the BBC report that due to the disruptions, temperatures in freezers rose, food spoiled, and some stores were forced to close their refrigerated sections. The European Commission called it, according to France 24, a deliberate attempt to disrupt the EU food chain. It is still unclear who is behind the attack, but the episode appears to be a continuation of a series of similar incidents.

health-and-inflation.summary: In different countries, news about disease and rising prices are appearing at the same time. In the United States, a child died of measles in New York — the first such death in 30 years — and the media link it to vaccination rates falling below the level needed to protect against outbreaks. In South Korea, October inflation came in at 2.8% and has remained close to the 2% range for the third month. Separately, Dawn writes that the authorities brought refineries in to help curb rising fuel prices. Taken together, this is presented as pressure on both health and household budgets.

south-korea-cybersecurity.title: South Korea is rushing to create a new cybersecurity center after a series of leaks and attacks
south-korea-cybersecurity.summary: South Korea is speeding up the creation of a nationwide cybersecurity center after a series of leaks and attacks. Reuters says President Lee Jae-myung ordered consideration of a powerful new agency, while Yonhap reports emergency checks at 2,100 government institutions and an urgent meeting after a data leak, including information about the president and his entourage. Separately, an investigation into the leak of data on passengers aboard the presidential aircraft is being reported. All this is happening against the backdrop of concerns about the country’s digital infrastructure and its economy.

Reuters and the FT report that China is pausing listings and asking banks to suspend IPOs in order to support weakened markets, while in the United States and Europe tech stocks and indexes are reacting to concerns over the AI boom. western-sahara-peacekeepers.title: The UN mission in Western Sahara has ended, while refugees await their return home
western-sahara-peacekeepers.summary: The UN mission in Western Sahara has ended after 35 years, as the Security Council did not extend its mandate. Africanews and the FT write that peacekeepers are leaving the disputed region, while analysts warn of the risk of escalation and a possible worsening of relations between Morocco and Algeria. Separate reports also speak of refugees’ hopes of returning home after a long wait. For now, uncertainty remains on the ground, and no political settlement has been reached.

fossil-red-blood-cells.summary: Scientists have reported traces of red blood cells in a dinosaur fossil from Brazil. Reuters writes about evidence of erythrocytes, while The Guardian notes that chemical tests in the Aratasaurus bone identified heme, an organic compound linked to oxygen transport in blood.
